stem:
Priya connects a nichrome wire to a cell in her school laboratory. After a few minutes, she notices that the wire has become warm.

Which statement correctly explains why the wire becomes warm?

options.text: The wire becomes warm simply because the cell is connected; current plays no part in heating.
The wire becomes warm first, and its warmth then makes the electric current flow through it.
Only nichrome wires become warm when an electric current flows; copper wires never do.
The current flowing through the wire meets resistance, and this resistance produces heat in the wire.

teacher.key_rationale: Heating of a current-carrying conductor is caused by resistance opposing the current, which converts electrical energy to heat; this matches option D. Option A omits the role of current and resistance, B reverses the cause-and-effect relationship, and C wrongly restricts heating to nichrome only.
